title: No one trains for 10 years
summary: Argues that people who claim a decade of training have rarely spent ten years on well-planned, consistent, serious training; breaks, skipped sessions and other goals eat that time. He says he started at 15 but has only trained seriously for bodybuilding for about two years, which is why he thinks natural potential is still largely unexplored and why ten real years of training would make anyone a master.

claims.claim: He started training at 15 and is 25, so he has 10 years of lifting, but breaks, skipped days and ineffective training made some periods worthless.
Almost no one actually spends 10 years on well-written, high-frequency programs without skipping days; this is one reason there are so few elite naturals.
He doesn't consider himself elite, or even advanced for most body parts, because he has only trained seriously for bodybuilding for about two years.
His first five years of lifting were for football and then basketball, focused on athletic ability; then he did powerlifting before turning to bodybuilding.
The earlier eight years built a lot of mass, but his results since getting serious about bodybuilding are incomparable, and he knows he's nowhere near his limits.
Life gets in the way of long-term consistency (illness, family, kids, marriage), and it's fine to re-prioritise sometimes.
Because almost no one trains seriously for a decade and YouTube fitness is young, human natural potential is still untouched; we may see things once thought impossible naturally.
The more advanced you are, the more program planning matters: 10 well-planned hours a week give completely different results from random lifts thrown together.
Many natural lifters give up and then wonder why they don't get results.
He never had good natural bodybuilding role models because the ones he found were on PEDs, which is partly why he made the channel.
Nothing would make him happier than seeing the next generation of naturals, some with better genetics than him, blow past what he achieved.
Unimpressive people who claim decades of training went to the gym for a decade; subtract the ineffective time and they didn't train that long.
He has only two years in bodybuilding but thousands of hours of hard work; hard work is not a talent, so it's accessible to everyone.
Ten real years of training in any skill or profession will make you a master.
